top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single, bounded invention (magic-wavelength trapping with Lamb-Dicke confinement of many neutral atoms) that is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, has been confirmed by independent laboratories at about 1e-18, and divides credit cleanly between Katori (concept and first realisation) and Ye (stability and accuracy), with no forced third name. Under a 'discovery or invention, not lifetime achievement' reading, two identifiable originators are responsible. P002 is prizeworthy and mature, but the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that guided the HgTe experiment cannot be honoured within three names, so its credit defect is harder to defend; it ranks above no award because the science is not in doubt.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the only listed connection is Chalmers co-affiliation with Goran Johansson, which is not a link to any candidate in the slate
